Class ChromaticText

java.lang.Object
net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.ChromaticText
public final class ChromaticText extends Object
Parses formatting instructions into visible glyphs and the style attached to each glyph.

The parser walks the original string once. Recognized instructions change its style state without producing letters. A visible Unicode code point produces a Glyph carrying the state at that point. Raw start/end positions still refer to the original string, so trimming can retain complete tokens instead of cutting through a bracket or hex sequence.

Width, trimming, wrapping and native rendering all use these same style decisions. The parser uses one definition snapshot for direct lookups; it does not draw anything or load client font classes. A width callback supplies the platform's actual character metrics.

    • advance

      public static float advance(float original, IChromaticEffect effect)
      Applies the layout-visible part of an effect to one normal character advance.

      Whole-segment transforms preserve normal flow width. Letter spacing adds its cushion. Other effects use a positive uniform scale sampled at the origin; nonpositive scale leaves the original advance intact. Visual x/y offsets do not change measured advance.

      Parameters:
      original - platform advance, including any vanilla bold expansion
      effect - current primary effect, or null
      Returns:
      adjusted advance; the unmodified original is returned for absent/whole-segment effects
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a sampled scale or computed adjusted advance is nonfinite

    • compile

      public static ChromaticText.Layout compile(String source)
      Parses a string using registered colors/effects, inline definitions and vanilla formatting.

      Both ampersand and section-sign markers are supported. Vanilla colors and reset clear custom state, while vanilla style flags retain it. Custom color tokens retain the primary effect, which may choose its own output color. Named tokens are scanned with a fixed definition-length bound. An unrecognized ampersand marker is emitted as text and scanning continues; an unknown section-sign pair is consumed and selects white with cleared styles.

      Ordinary character lookup tries effect, color, then outline. Bracketed lookup tries a registered named effect, named color, enabled inline effect, then named outline. Bracket and hex syntax branches run before ordinary character lookup. Direct registered lookups use one captured definition snapshot.

      Parameters:
      source - non-null input text with optional formatting instructions
      Returns:
      layout retaining visible Unicode code points and original source offsets
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if source is null
